chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the ornaments; is there Zakat upon them? He said: No.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Is there Zakat on gold and silver jewelry in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Shia juristic consensus that Zakat is not obligatory on personal jewelry (al-huliy), distinguishing it from trade goods or raw wealth. It reflects the broader Shia legal principle that adornments intended for personal use are exempt from the annual alms-tax, a ruling derived from the Imams' clarification of Quranic obligations. This specific narration highlights the practical application of fiqh regarding the distinction between consumption/use and accumulation/investment.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked himasws about the ornaments, ‘Is there Zakāt regarding it?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from ibn Muskan from Muhammad al- Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Zakat and jewelry.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Zakat is not due on jewelries.”’
